features.note: Regression check after blade darkening: counter-rotation survives. At 30% the top blade hoods forward with a lit bluish top skin, the drive blade sweeps opposite with a soft-gradient mid-grey curved face, the bottom blade counter-tilts with its own lit top skin; adjacent blades never read parallel. Pulling the blade into the galv family did NOT flatten the opposed read — the three blades still separate by orientation-driven shading, not by value clipping.

Improved: plated stub clearly protrudes from the frame right face ahead of the black U-clamp; orange body hangs on the shaft, never flush; anti-rotation strap drops to a frame foot. The compositional weakness from attempt 1 is gone — the UI panel no longer abuts the actuator and the full hero corner (stub, clamp, body, label, cable gland) reads with clear air around it.

Round dial with pale printed face, bezel and bold dark pointer visible on the actuator head; pointer angle consistent with 30% travel. Arc printing still not resolvable at this frame size — the gauge reads by bezel/pointer shape. Marginal but above threshold; unchanged from attempt 1.

No regression: real ~0.13 m channel depth, flange plates on both faces with discrete fasteners, visible wall thickness at the opening. Galv mottle breaks up the flats; with the lifted background the far flange edge now separates from the void instead of dissolving.

No regression: plated vertical tie rod with crank blocks on the left (non-actuator) side picks up clean edge highlights, and against the lighter slate background the rod silhouette reads more easily than in attempt 1. Crank blocks remain dim but discernible; spacing consistent with 30% travel.

important_features.note: Improved by the blade-value fix: the near-black EPDM strips along the blade meeting lines now read as discrete dark bulbs against mid-grey blades rather than merging into a crushed band. Upper jamb seal still partially merges with the residual dark upper-left interior corner.
Structured printed plate (header, model line, spec rows, barcode) on the orange body survives the revised rig without blowing out; reads as a factory label at natural scale.

Clearly improved: the cable now exits the gland and drops fully visible — no UI clipping — with a readable bend/sag against the lighter lower-right background. It terminates in mid-air short of the ground plane, so the catenary read is good but not perfect.

defects: Residual from correction 1 (partially landed): the upper-left interior corner behind the top blade still crushes to near-black — the fill lifts the upper interior band enough for the seals to separate, but the corner pocket and the deepest jamb still bottom out; minor, no longer the dominant read.

Depth fog is subtle: object-vs-void separation is now real (floor-to-void gradient, grounded shadow), but near-flange vs far-flange atmospheric separation is still carried mostly by geometry and the background lift, not by visible depth attenuation.
Cable catenary ends in mid-air above the ground plane rather than reaching a surface or exit point; plausible but slightly unresolved at the tail.
Single-view ambiguity (per gate contract): one neutral view only, no grazing/reference-match companions in this attempt; all scores capped at 0.85.
corrections: Optional polish (non-blocking): feather a touch more fill or AO falloff into the upper-left interior corner so the pocket behind the top blade reads above black without brightening the EPDM seals.
Optional polish (non-blocking): give the cable tail a termination (reach the floor shadow zone or coil at a junction) so the catenary resolves instead of ending mid-air.
For any future material/lighting re-gate, produce the look-dev triple (neutral + grazing + reference-match) so scores can be confirmed above the single-view 0.85 cap.
